key_insight: The paper proposes steering neural network training with interpretable partial-dependence constraints so the model’s average feature response matches prior domain knowledge.
engineering_relevance: This enables more data-efficient regression models whose explanations are both faithful to expert expectations and useful for guiding engineering decisions.
method: Compute partial dependence of selected inputs during training.
Add constraints so the learned average response follows user-specified functional knowledge.
Optimize the neural network under these explanation-guided objectives.
evidence_signal: Across several regression benchmarks, including dynamical systems forecasting, constrained models outperformed unconstrained ones and used data more efficiently while producing interpretations aligned with the provided knowledge.
watch_item: The approach depends on having reliable prior functional knowledge and well-chosen feature-level constraints, which may be difficult to specify in complex real-world systems.
paper_title: Steering Neural Network Training through Interpretable Constraints Based on Partial Dependence
